A.explanation: Velocity is $+1 \text{m s}^{-1}$ from 0 to 2 s, zero from 2 to 4 s, $-2 \text{m s}^{-1}$ from 4 to 6 s, then zero, matching the slopes of the displacement graph.

B.explanation: The first velocity step is too large at $2 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and the negative step from 4 to 6 s is too small in magnitude for a $4 \text{m}$ fall in $2 \text{s}$.

C.explanation: The signs are reversed, showing negative velocity when displacement is rising from 0 to 2 s and positive velocity when displacement is falling from 4 to 6 s.

D.explanation: The 4 to 6 s section is shown as positive velocity, but displacement decreases from $2 \text{m}$ to $-2 \text{m}$ so velocity must be negative there.

hints: Notice the four straight sections of the displacement-time graph: rising 0 to 2 s, flat 2 to 4 s, steeply falling 4 to 6 s, flat 6 to 10 s.
Recall velocity is the gradient $v = \Delta x / \Delta t$, so flat sections give $v = 0$ and a falling displacement gives negative $v$.
Compare the steepness: the $2 \text{m}$ rise in $2 \text{s}$ gives $+1 \text{m s}^{-1}$, while the $4 \text{m}$ fall in $2 \text{s}$ gives $-2 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify velocity as the gradient of the displacement-time graph using $v = \Delta x / \Delta t$.
From $2$ to $4 \text{s}$ displacement stays at $2 \text{m}$, so $\Delta x = 0$ and $v = 0$.
From $4$ to $6 \text{s}$ displacement falls from $2 \text{m}$ to $-2 \text{m}$, so $\Delta x = -4 \text{m}$ and $v = -4/2 = -2 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
From $6$ to $10 \text{s}$ displacement stays at $-2 \text{m}$, so $v = 0$.
The sequence $+1$, $0$, $-2$, $0$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ over the same time intervals matches graph A. This is option A
